title: gmellon: headless gnome-keyring unlock CLI
description: Every unlock door on this SSH-only machine is shut: gcr-prompter needs X/Wayland; 'gnome-keyring-daemon --unlock' never forwards to a running (systemd socket-activated) daemon; pam_gnome_keyring is not installed and only fires on password logins; secret-tool deliberately has no unlock command; the Secret Service Unlock() call is prompt-gated. The daemon's private control protocol (OP_UNLOCK/OP_CHANGE on $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/keyring/control) is the one interface that accepts a password from any client of ours — pam_gnome_keyring speaks it, gmellon is its shell-native sibling. Full spec in README.md (readme-driven development: README is the source of truth).
acceptance_criteria: gmellon unlock and gmellon change work against a real throwaway daemon (harness-verified), with TTY/stdin-only password input, --allow-create guard against unlock-or-create landmine, spec exit codes, and README-matching --help.
